Mandated Reporter: This position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter pursuant to the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and requires immediate reporting of physical abuse, sexual abuse, emotional abuse, or neglect of anyone under the age of 18. It is the responsibility of the Mandated Reporter to ensure that they obtain proper training in order to fulfill their reporting responsibilities as required by the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and University policy, and to complete and submit the required reports to the UC San Diego Police Department without delay.
Demonstrated experience to interpret and apply complex rules and policies in relation to events.

Under the direction of the Associate Director, Artistic Programs & Operations, the Guest Services Coordinator leads the day-to-day guest experience at the Strauss Family Gallery (the Strauss), the Chief Campus Curator’s Office’s free, open-to-the-public gallery of contemporary art. The Strauss is designed as a third space: visitors are free to come and go, and are encouraged to stay, work, study, and connect with the art and with each other.

The Coordinator is responsible for how visitors enter, move through, and engage with the space, and for cultivating an atmosphere that supports both quiet use and active engagement. The Coordinator hires, trains, schedules, and provides work direction to a docent team made up of student workers and community volunteers; serves as the primary point of contact for guest requests, complaints, and accessibility needs; and maintains a safe, welcoming, and well-run public environment. Working from exhibition content provided by the curatorial team, the Coordinator builds and delivers docent training and visitor engagement standards. The Coordinator supports the Public Engagement team by preparing the space for programs and events, and coordinates rentals, vendors, and outside groups when the Strauss is used for external events.

Because the Strauss is newly opening, the Coordinator will design, implement, and manage, in coordination with the Associate Director, the systems used to assess the guest experience and to track attendance, engagement, and other metrics, and will report findings to CCCO leadership. As the office grows, the scope of this role may expand to guest services across other CCCO sites and initiatives.
Cover letter is required for application to be considered complete.
Demonstrated ability to work independently, identify problems and recommend solutions.
Demonstrated ability at presenting a positive, professional and helpful impression and working as a team member.Skill in de-escalation, conflict resolution, and service recovery with the public.
Strong computer skills to include wording processing, spreadsheets, database management systems and the web. Ability to operate both Macintosh and IBM computers.

Skill in conceptualizing, planning and organizing events and projects. Proven skill in arranging logistics, producing materials, participant registration, billing and problem solving, and ability to close sales.

Excellent customer service skills. Ability to communicate in a helpful, pleasant and informative manner to a wide variety of people, both in person and on the telephone. Demonstrated ability to effectively handle heavy telephone volume and solve customer needs and problems.
Ability to work independently and make decisions (based on standard operating procedures) with minimum of instruction and supervision.
Familiarity with special event planning, equipment and set-up logistics as related to parking services and traffic management.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate with a diverse group of people including vendors, faculty, staff and students.
Demonstrated ability to reorganize schedules quickly to effectively manage rapidly changing priorities and/or emergencies in a busy environment.

Ability to provide best in class customer service demonstrating patience, professionalism, and kindness in all interactions with guests and colleagues. Exceptional communication skills with the ability to interact positively with a diverse group of people.
Demonstrated ability to work independently and respond to complaints, comments, facility problems, medical or other emergencies, always acting in accordance with university & OSHA policies.
Knowledge of visitor services and front-of-house practices in a museum, gallery, or comparable cultural or public venue, including visitor flow, wayfinding, and gallery etiquette.
